root_idea.summary: The root centers on harm, injury, damage, and detriment.
root_idea.development: The noun ضَيْر denotes harm or detriment, while the related verb ضَارَهُ means to harm, injure, or damage, and is equated with ضَرَّهُ and أَضَرَّ بِهِ.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested noun with an independently supported lexical meaning.

senses.usage_conditions: Occurs in the Quranic construction لَا ضَيْرَ, meaning “there is no harm” or “no harm will befall.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To harm, injure, hurt, damage, or do mischief to someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; also reported with the imperfect يَضِيرُ or يَضُورُ and the verbal nouns ضَيْرٌ and ضَوْرٌ. Equivalent to ضَرَّهُ or أَضَرَّ بِهِ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers the noun ضَيْر for harm and the related verb ضَارَهُ meaning to harm or damage.

cautions: The Quranic noun is attested once, in لَا ضَيْرَ. The cited evidence for آل عمران 3:120 concerns a related verb form and does not constitute a second occurrence of this noun.
